It's already happening.

Not a far-off disaster. Ordinary disruption that lasts long enough to matter.

  1. 25 October 2026More than 57,000 homes lose power in a stormIncluding homes in Greater Manchester, Cumbria and Lancashire. 1news, citing Sky News
  2. 28 September 2026A burst main cuts water to 6,000 propertiesNo time was given for the fix. People queued at bottled water stations. Newswav
  3. January 2025Floods force over 1,000 people from their homes in Greater ManchesterA major incident, followed by a cold weather alert. Hits Radio
  4. December 2015Lancaster loses power for four daysFloodwater hit a substation and more than 61,000 homes and businesses went dark. Cash machines, petrol stations, mobiles and the internet stopped. FM radio kept working. What Lancaster teaches us
  5. 3 November 2026The UK's cyber agency warns power and water systems will be targetedIt says AI-powered attacks on critical infrastructure are "highly likely" by 2028. National Security News

The government now asks every home to manage for three days.

In October 2026 the Cabinet Office launched Be Ready, asking households to keep enough water and food to look after themselves for three days. GOV.UK

Why three days? The BBC reports that the National Energy System Operator's latest advice is that, after a national failure, power could probably be restored in two to three days.

The UK's Chief Medical Officers have also written the radio scripts they would read out if the whole country lost power: don't flush the toilet, drink at least 2 litres a day, eat chilled food first. Read what they'd say.

But the checklist is the same for everyone. A family on the ninth floor with a baby and an electric hob needs a very different plan from a couple in a house with a gas hob and a garden.

Flat, 9th floor

2 adults, a baby on formula, electric hob, no garden

  1. Ready-made formula. No power means no way to boil water for powder.
  2. 27 litres of water, stored now. The building's pumps need electricity.
  3. No-cook food only. Nowhere safe to use a camping stove.

House with a garden

2 adults, gas hob, gas central heating

  1. A carbon monoxide alarm. Gas appliances, and the temptation to cook indoors.
  2. Blankets and a warm room. The gas boiler stops without electricity.
  3. Matches by the hob. The gas may still work, the spark won't.

That's why Fettle starts with your home, not a generic list.

Most of us aren't there yet.

The government's own 2026 survey of over 10,000 people found:

  • 82% have less than one day of bottled water at home.
  • 14% have a household emergency plan.
  • 21% have none of the basics on the government's list.
  • 73% in England and Wales have never heard of their Local Resilience Forum.

Source: Cabinet Office, UK Public Survey of Risk Perception, Resilience and Preparedness 2026

Fettle for Communities For councils, housing providers and support teams

The people most at risk are the least likely to download an app.

Older people living alone. People who rely on oxygen or a powered bed. Families with a new baby in temporary housing. People who don't read English well. Fettle gives your frontline staff a 10-minute visit that ends with a real plan and a printed book.

  • Supported visits. Staff go through the questions with the resident, after a consent script they read aloud.
  • A printed book for every home, in English, Polish, Romanian, Panjabi or Urdu, with large print for older residents.
  • Priority Services Register sign-ups done on the visit, and counted.
  • Progress you can report. Readiness at the first visit and at the check-in, by household and by ward.
  • Anonymous ward totals for emergency planners: who relies on powered equipment, who lives alone, who's high up. Small numbers are always hidden.
  • Training for frontline staff, and a home visit checklist.

Questions

Is this official advice?

Fettle is independent. Everything we recommend comes from official UK sources, which we link to, and we turn it into a plan for your home. In an emergency, always follow official alerts.

Do I have to buy lots of stuff?

No. Many of the most important jobs are free, like joining the Priority Services Register. The rest is spread over months at a budget you choose. We never sell a doomsday kit.

I rent, or live in a flat. Is it still for me?

Yes. Flats, especially high up, have their own risks, like water pumps and lifts that need power. The plan takes that into account.

What do you do with my health answers?

They're optional, only used to build your plan, and never shared or sold. If a council or charity worker helps you make your plan, they can see it too. Only if you agree, your answers are counted in anonymous totals for your area, and small numbers are always hidden.

Is Fettle in other languages?

Yes. Fettle and The Fettle Book are available in English, Polish, Romanian, Panjabi and Urdu. Choose your language at the top of the page.

Can I make a plan for my mum?

Yes. Add another household, with their agreement, and keep both plans in one place.

Do you earn money from products you suggest?

Yes, sometimes. Some product suggestions are Amazon links, marked "paid link". As an Amazon Associate, Fettle earns from qualifying purchases, at no extra cost to you. It never changes what we recommend, and you can buy anywhere. The printed book has no shopping links.
